九尾がひらく夜、願いの底へ。: Beneath nine unfurled tails, descend into the heart of a wish.
今宵も、あの姫に逢うために。: Tonight, we return to see her once more.
覚醒核はこの難易度だけ。道中の消耗を抑え、薬と役割を整えて九尾に挑む。: Awakening Cores drop only here. Conserve your strength on the way, prepare potions and roles, and face the Nine-Tailed Princess.
葛葉の契りを集め、妖狐の姫を仲間に迎える。: Gather Kuzuha's covenant fragments and welcome the fox princess into your party.
月翅の群れを抜け、星の欠片を拾う。: Pass through moonlit wings and gather fallen stars.
月の光が降り積もる庭。月翅の蛾と白霧の狼を越え、最後に月翅の主へ挑む。全体攻撃を: A garden dusted with moonlight. Defeat Moon Moths and Pale Wolves before facing the lord of the wings. A short, two-wave route suited to area attacks. Earn one Wishstone every clear.
癒しの祈りが響く回廊を、ひと息に。: Press through the cloister before its healing prayers return.
白い花が導く祈りの道。帳の巫女が狼を癒し、奥では巫女自身が道を守る。攻撃重視で回: White flowers mark a path of prayer. A Veiled Priestess heals the wolves, then guards the way herself. Overcome her healing in this short, two-wave route. Earn one Wishstone every clear.
石燐の鱗と銀の鎧、その先の灯へ。: Beyond stoneglow scales and silver armor, a lantern waits.
銀灯が揺れる古い門。石燐の幼竜と荊の魔女を越え、虚ろの守り手と向き合う。回復を織: An ancient gate lit by silver lanterns. Defeat a Stone Drake and Thorn Witch, then face the Hollow Guardian. Balance healing with sustained offense over two waves. Earn one Wishstone every clear.
神々も、今宵は黒いレースを纏う。: Tonight, even the gods wear black lace.
よくいらしたわ。今宵は、どんな願いを預けるの？: Welcome. What wish will you entrust to me tonight?
ふふ……その眼差し、少し気に入ったわ。: Hehe… I am beginning to like that look in your eyes.
また逢いにきて。契りの続きは、その時に。: Come see me again. We shall continue our covenant then.
九つの尾がほどける夜。もう、夢からは帰さない。: On the night my nine tails unfurl, even dreams will not lead you home.
ここまで追ってくるなんて……本気にしてしまうわ。: You followed me this far… You might make me take this seriously.
あなたの願い、九つの尾に結びましょう。: Let us bind your wish to these nine tails.
……ここから先は、夢さえ帰れない。: …Beyond this point, even dreams cannot return.
まだ、その灯を消すわけにはいかない。: I cannot let that light go out. Not yet.
ようやく……あの人の足音が、聞こえる。: At last… I can hear those footsteps again.
この庭の眠りを、誰が呼び覚ました。: Who has disturbed this garden's sleep?
石は砕けても……約束は、残る。: Stone may shatter… but a promise remains.
花を……踏まないで、おくれ。: Please… do not tread on the flowers.
名を捨てた者だけが、この門を守れる。: Only those who abandon their names may guard this gate.
主よ……もう少しだけ、お待ちください。: My liege… please wait just a little longer.
鍵を、あなたに。今度こそ……扉の向こうへ。: The key is yours. This time… beyond the door.
欠けた月の夢を、あなたにも。: May you, too, dream beneath the waning moon.
夜明けなど……来なくても、よかったのに。: Perhaps… dawn need never have come.
この祈りだけは、奪わないで。: Please, do not take this prayer from me.
届かないと知っても……私は、祈る。: Even knowing it cannot reach them… I will pray.
こんなにも静かに……終われるのですね。: So this is how quietly… it can end.
枯れた花にも、帰る場所はある。: Even withered flowers have a place to return to.
咲かせましょう……最後の、一輪を。: Let it bloom… one final flower.
庭のこと……ときどき、思い出して。: Remember the garden… once in a while.
誰もいない礼拝堂に、今日も花を供える祈り手。救えなかった人々の名を、彼女だけがま: She still lays flowers in an empty chapel. Only she remembers the names of those she could not save. Beneath her gentle voice lies a quiet resolve never to let go of another hand.
滅びた王国の門を守り続けた騎士。主のいない盾は重さを失わず、彼女はその重さを生き: A knight who still guards the gate of a fallen kingdom. Her masterless shield has never grown lighter; she has made its weight a reason to live. A woman of few words, she never forgets to match her companions' pace.
朝の来ない街で剣を振るう旅人。彼女の刃は、過ぎ去ったものへの弔いであり、まだ見ぬ: A traveler who carries her sword through a city without morning. Her blade mourns what has passed and points toward a tomorrow still unseen. She gazes at rain-washed cobblestones as though remembering another life.
消えた星座を読み続ける魔術師。崩れた天文台から持ち出した一冊の本には、誰にも見え: A mage who still reads constellations that have vanished. The book she rescued from a ruined observatory records a sky no one else can see. At night, she teaches her companions the forgotten names of stars.
聖堂に迷い込んだ魂を、出口まで導く白い獣。その足跡は霧とともに消える。かつて誰か: A white beast that guides lost souls out of the cathedral. Its footprints dissolve into mist. It once waited for someone, they say, but can no longer remember their face.
崩れた噴水の底で長い眠りについていた竜。石のような鱗の隙間から、青白い光がこぼれ: A drake long asleep beneath a broken fountain. Pale blue light seeps between its stone-like scales. It walks with surprising care, unwilling to crush even the smallest flower.
錆銀の鎧に名前を隠した女騎士。朽ちた鍵束を腰に下げ、閉じるべき扉を探している。鎧: A woman knight whose name is hidden behind tarnished armor. With old keys at her waist, she searches for doors that should be closed. Inside the armor, a tiny, faded ribbon is still carefully sewn in place.
月明かりの差す場所にだけ現れる幻の蛾。翅に散る燐粉は、触れた者に遠い夢を見せる。: An elusive moth that appears only in moonlight. Dust from its wings brings dreams of distant places. Some say it carries the words of the dead; others believe it is the loneliness of the living given form.
破れた聖歌を口ずさむ、角を持つ女性。人々が去った後も祈りの灯を絶やさなかった。差: A horned woman who hums a broken hymn. Long after the people left, she kept the light of prayer alive. When she takes an offered hand, her cold fingers tremble ever so slightly.
花を咲かせなくなった庭に暮らす魔女。荊の冠は罰ではなく、彼女自身が選んだ約束のし: A witch who lives in a garden where flowers no longer bloom. Her crown of thorns is a promise she chose, not a punishment. Whenever someone brings her seeds, the corners of her mouth soften into a smile.
神楽の舞台で、赤茶の短い髪と紅いリボンを弾ませる女神。神楽鈴を高く掲げ、扇を開き: A goddess whose short auburn hair and red ribbon sway across the kagura stage. She raises her sacred bells and opens her fan, dancing in black and ivory gothic lace. She believes laughter can return even to a city sealed in silence.
富士を背に、桜の枝と小さな炎をそっと掲げる女神。桜色と黒いレースのゴシックロリー: With Mount Fuji behind her, she holds a cherry branch and a small flame. Dressed in pink and black gothic lace, she plays with sparks as though they were petals. Her prayers, knowing both fragility and strength, quietly keep her companions alive.
岩戸の向こうから朝を連れてくる女神。黒髪のボブに太陽の光輪を戴き、白と黒のフリル: A goddess who brings morning from beyond the heavenly cave. A solar halo crowns her dark bob, and gold adorns her black-and-white gothic frills. When the Yata Mirror catches dawn, warmth returns even to the shuttered city.
黄泉の境界に立つ女神が、銀髪を黒い喪のヴェールで包み、黒と紫のゴシックロリータを: At the boundary of Yomi, a goddess veils her silver hair in black mourning lace. She wears gothic frills of black and violet, a magatama at her breast, and carries red spider lilies and an old lantern. Before a sealed rock, she now chooses to protect the companions beside her.
宵宮の妖狐姫: Fox Princess of the Dusk Shrine
参拝者の途絶えた稲荷の社で、今も人々の願いを預かる妖狐の姫。紅の結び紐と古い鈴は: At an abandoned Inari shrine, a fox princess still accepts people's wishes. Every red cord and old bell marks another forgotten covenant. The smile behind her fan hides both the pleasure of testing visitors and the loneliness of waiting for someone.
月が欠ける夜、封じた九つの尾と白銀の髪が本来の姿を取り戻す。揺れる狐火は、守りき: Under an eclipsed moon, her silver hair and nine sealed tails regain their true form. Each wandering foxfire remembers a wish she could not protect. Yet she quietly writes your name—the one who chose to stand beside her—upon her final binding cord.
羽音だけが静寂を渡る。: Only the sound of wings crosses the silence.
眠れる水底に、青い灯。: A blue light sleeps beneath the water.
届かぬ聖歌の、その先へ。: Beyond a hymn that never reaches its listeners.
枯れた花々の名前を呼ぶ。: Call the names of flowers long withered.
最後の鍵は、まだ冷たい。: The last key is still cold.
頁に残された月の匂い。: The scent of moonlight lingers on its pages.
もう見えない星を探して。: Search for stars no longer visible.
ここで、ひとつの祈りが終わる。: Here, a single prayer comes to an end.

遠き地の女神たちが、自ら選んだ晴れ着で月下の花宴へ。: Goddesses from distant lands join a moonlit flower banquet in kimono of their choosing.
傷ついた味方2人を、各々単体回復の半分の威力で同時回復。負傷者が2人以上のときに: Heals two wounded allies at half the power of a single-target heal each. Used when at least two allies are wounded; prioritizes a single-target heal for an ally near defeat.
敵1体の障壁を破壊してから控えめな攻撃。障壁がある敵へ使用し、かばうがあれば引き: Shatters one enemy's barrier before a modest attack. Used against shielded enemies. If intercepted, shatters the guardian's barrier instead.
敵1体の攻撃強化と再生を同時に解除。該当する効果がある敵へ優先使用。ダメージは与: Removes Attack Up and Regen from one enemy, prioritizing enemies with these effects. Deals no damage and does not remove barriers, guarding, or leader effects.
初回SSR保証は使用済みです。以降は共通90回天井です。: Your one-time introductory SSR guarantee has been used. The shared 90-wish guarantee now applies.
次の祈願で、全ガチャ共通・一度きりの初回SSR保証を使用します。: Your next wish uses the one-time introductory SSR guarantee shared across all collections.
全ガチャを合計して2回目だけ、初回SSR保証を使用できます。: The introductory SSR guarantee applies only to your second wish in total across all collections.
シリーズを切り替えても、祈願回数とSSR天井の進行は引き継ぎます。初回保証はシリ: Wish totals and SSR pity carry over when switching collections. Switching does not renew the introductory guarantee.
SSR未獲得90回目でSSR確定。74回目からSSR率が1回ごとに6ポイント上昇: An SSR is guaranteed by your 90th wish without one. From wish 74, SSR odds rise by 6 percentage points per wish. Receiving any SSR resets pity to zero.
一度きりの初回SSR保証を使いますか？: Use your one-time introductory SSR guarantee?
この祈願で、全ガチャ共通の初回SSR保証を消費します。他のシリーズでは再使用でき: This wish consumes your introductory SSR guarantee across ALL collections. It cannot be used again in another collection. Later wishes follow the shared 90-wish SSR guarantee.
石5個を消費して、選択中のシリーズのSSRを1人迎えます。重複する場合があります: Spend 5 Wishstones to receive one SSR from this collection. It may be a duplicate. Canceling spends neither stones nor the guarantee.
全ガチャ共通の初回SSR保証を使用しました: One-time introductory SSR guarantee used across all collections
ギリシャ神話の月の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。月白と紺の振袖を自ら選び、銀糸: A flower-banquet guest inspired by the moon goddess of Greek mythology. She chose a moonwhite and midnight-blue furisode embroidered with silver crescents. Opening her moonlit fan fills the garden with gentle protective light. She quietly makes sure every guest can enjoy the evening.
ギリシャ神話の知恵の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。藍の羽織にはオリーブの枝と梟: A flower-banquet guest inspired by the goddess of wisdom in Greek mythology. Olive branches and owls adorn her indigo haori. Delighted by the ingenuity of woven patterns, she listens closely to her companions' stories. On their travels, clear judgment and steadfast protection guide the party onward.
ローマ神話の花の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。桜色と若草色の晴れ着に、牡丹や小: A flower-banquet guest inspired by the flower goddess of Roman mythology. Peonies and tiny wildflowers adorn her rose-pink and fresh-green kimono. She learns the name of every garden flower and offers small bouquets to those she meets. Her gentle blossom breeze tends her companions' wounds and ailments.
ギリシャ神話の虹と伝令の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。雲と流水を織り込んだ袖が: A flower-banquet guest inspired by the rainbow and messenger goddess of Greek mythology. Clouds and flowing water grace sleeves that shimmer in soft rainbow colors. Carrying replies to the invitation with care, she shares stories from distant lands. In battle, she encourages her companions and clears away enemy enhancements.
海竜の姫が、深藍の絹と真珠のレースを纏って陸の月を見上げる。珊瑚の角と二筋の潮は: A sea-dragon princess gazes at the moon above the land, dressed in deep-blue silk and pearl lace. Coral horns and twin currents recall the sea palace she cannot return to. Water gathered in her shell cup embraces two wounded companions without distinction.
人の途絶えた機殿で、今日も朝の光を織り続ける女神。琥珀の髪に挿した小さな杼は、消: A goddess keeps weaving morning light in an abandoned weaving hall. A tiny shuttle in her amber hair binds fading wishes anew. Gold thread edging her black lace draws out her companions' strength, while a soft woven ward receives approaching blades.
花の散った後も山を守る、永い命の女神。翡翠の瞳と短い石灰色の髪、重たい黒の衣に小: A goddess of enduring life guards the mountains after the blossoms fall. Small alpine flowers adorn her heavy black dress, beneath jade eyes and short limestone-gray hair. She transforms memories of rejection into a shield for her companions and a stone scepter that breaks false barriers.
生と黄泉の境に架かる橋で、こじれた願いの結び目をほどく女神。銅赤の三つ編みと水引: On a bridge between life and the underworld, a goddess gently untangles knotted wishes. The silver scissors in her copper-red braid are not meant to sever bonds. She loosens only the threads of enemy power and regeneration, opening a path for her companions.
専用素材は合成・分解できません。: Exclusive materials cannot be combined or dismantled.
この花を、誰に渡すはずだったのでしょう。: Who was I meant to give this flower to?
忘れても、約束はここに。: Even if I forget, the promise remains here.
セリス……一緒に、帰りましょう。: Seris… let us go home together.
命令より、帰る者を守る。: I protect those returning home, above any order.
帰還の許可なら、とうに出ている。: Permission to return was granted long ago.
消えた名前を、もう一度読ませて。: Let me read the vanished name once more.
朝の記録は、まだ終わらない。: The record of morning is not over yet.
余白には、あなたの名前を。: Your name belongs in the margin.
救ったものを、その手で失う覚悟はある？: Are you prepared to lose, by your own hand, what you saved?
あの夜を、繰り返させはしない。: I will not let that night happen again.
……最後の稽古は、隣を歩くことにしましょう。: …For our final lesson, let us walk side by side.
あの日の剣を、今度こそ越えて。: This time, surpass the sword of that day.
ひとりで夜を引き受けるのは、もう終わり。: You no longer have to bear the night alone.
約束の朝へ。一緒に、帰ろう。: Toward the promised dawn. Let us go home together.
弔鐘の剣姫: Sword Maiden of the Passing Bell
セリスに剣を教えた女性。割れた鐘の耳飾りを揺らし、夜明けへの道を塞ぐ。あの子に教: The woman who taught Seris the sword blocks the way to dawn, a cracked bell earring swaying. There is one stance she never taught her pupil: how to stop someone returning home without cutting them down.
余分な一輪は弔いではなく、帰還の約束だった。白花を携え、今度は自分も朝へ向かう。: The extra flower was a promise of return, never an offering of mourning. Carrying white blossoms, she now walks toward morning herself.
盾のひびを金で継ぎ、門の外で仲間を待つ騎士。守るべきものを、自分の意志で選び直し: A knight waits outside the gate, the cracks in her shield mended with gold. She has chosen anew, of her own will, what she will protect.
星図の余白に、共に歩む者たちの名を書き足した。誰か一人を代償にする計算は、もう必: She added the names of her fellow travelers to the margins of her star chart. No calculation need demand a single person's sacrifice anymore.
弟子を夜に留める剣を下ろし、隣を歩く師。金で継いだ鐘は、弔いではなく朝の合図にな: The teacher lowers the sword that kept her pupil in the night and walks beside her. The bell mended with gold now signals morning, not mourning.
雨上がりの石畳を、彼女はもう懐かしそうには眺めない。その先へ、一緒に歩く人がいる: She no longer gazes at the rain-washed cobblestones with longing. Someone is there to walk with her beyond them.
薄明の剣と、約束の朝: The Twilight Sword and the Promised Dawn
四つの記憶が、夜の向こうで彼女を待つ。: Four memories await her beyond the night.
朝の来ない街で剣を振るう旅人。雨上がりの石畳を、いつも懐かしそうに眺めている。彼: A traveler wields her sword in a city where morning never comes. She gazes at rain-washed cobblestones with longing. A single crack darker than night runs through her blade.
礼拝堂の白花、門の鍵、星図の余白、遠い鐘。知らないはずのものに触れるたび、剣を握: White flowers in the chapel, a gate key, the margins of a star chart, a distant bell. Whenever she touches something she should not recognize, her sword hand stills. "I feel as though I promised someone we would go home together."
街が滅びる朝を、彼女は剣で切り離した。人々を守った夜は、やがて名前まで奪っていっ: With her sword, she cut away the morning that would destroy the city. The night that protected its people eventually stole even their names. The four companions recovered no miracle, but a promise to face tomorrow together. She no longer gazes at rain-washed cobblestones with longing. Someone is there to walk with her beyond them.
礼拝堂の花は、いつも一輪だけ多い。誰のためか尋ねると、彼女は旅人の剣を見た。: There is always one extra flower in the chapel. Asked whom it is for, she looks at the traveler's sword.
旅立ちの日、エレインはセリスに花を渡さなかった。「帰ったら、一緒に摘みましょう」: On the day they departed, Elaine gave Seris no flower. "When we return, let us pick them together." Those words alone keep returning to her lips in the middle of prayer.
朝を封じに行くセリスを、彼女は止められなかった。だから残した一輪は弔いではない。: She could not stop Seris from going to seal away morning. The flower she left was therefore no token of mourning. "This time, I am coming too. So we remember the flowers' names on our way home." For the first time, the white blossom awaits morning dew.
門を破った傷は、外側にはひとつもない。錆銀の騎士は、鍵を誰にも預けない。: There is not a single mark of the breached gate on its outer side. The tarnished-silver knight entrusts its key to no one.
最後の勅命は、城門を閉ざすことだった。リオラはその命令書を盾の裏に隠している。折: The final royal command was to close the city gate. Liora keeps the order hidden behind her shield. Beyond its folds, only Seris's footprints remain.
あの夜、門を内側から開いたのはリオラだった。王国への誓いより、帰ってくる一人を選: That night, Liora opened the gate from within. Over her oath to the kingdom, she chose the one person who would return. Raising her shield mended with gold, she waits for Seris outside the gate this time. "Permission to return was granted long ago."
彼女の本には、一夜分だけ朝の記録がある。末尾の名前は、何度も書き直されていた。: Her book contains a record of morning for just one night. The name at its end has been rewritten many times.
星図に朝を描くたび、同じ場所のインクが消える。ノエルはそこにセリスの名を書き、消: Whenever she draws morning onto the star chart, the ink in the same place fades. Noelle writes Seris's name there and reads it aloud before it vanishes.
封印を解けば、街は止められていた滅びと再び向き合う。ノエルはそれを知り、一人に代: Breaking the seal means facing the destruction that was held at bay. Knowing this, Noelle abandoned any calculation that would demand one person's sacrifice. When she added four names to the star chart's margins, the vanished morning star returned.
あの子に教えなかった構えがある。帰る者を、斬らずに止める構えだ。割れた鐘の耳飾り: There is one stance she never taught the girl: how to stop someone returning home without cutting them down. Her cracked bell earring rang in the windless night.
セリスに剣を教えた女は、夜明けへの道を塞いだ。「救ったものを、その手で失う覚悟は: The woman who taught Seris the sword blocked the way to dawn. "Are you prepared to lose, by your own hand, what you saved?" The question's point turned more toward herself than her pupil.
弟子に街の命運を背負わせたまま、師は夜の終わりを恐れていた。弔鐘のひびを金で継ぎ: Having left the city's fate on her pupil's shoulders, the teacher feared the night's end. Mending the passing bell with gold, Lisette lowered her sword. "Your final lesson. This time, walk beside me." The bell now signals morning, not mourning.
白霧の足跡は、礼拝堂から門へ続く。: White-mist pawprints lead from the chapel to the gate.
狼は紺の外套の裾を嗅ぐと、雨上がりの道に伏せた。帰る者を待つ仕草だった。: The wolf sniffed the hem of the navy cloak, then lay down on the rain-washed road. It was waiting for someone to return.
霧の向こうに、まだ名を呼ぶ声が残っている。: Beyond the mist, a voice still calls a name.
枯園の荊には、白い布の切れ端が結ばれている。: A scrap of white cloth is tied to a thorn in the withered garden.
「あの剣が朝を斬った日から、種は芽を出す夢ばかり見る」。魔女は新しい鉢を窓辺に置: "Since that sword cut away morning, the seeds dream only of sprouting." The witch placed a new pot by the window.
その鉢は、まだ誰のためとも呼ばれていない。: No one has yet said whom that pot is for.
花を一輪、残した理由。: The reason one flower was left behind.
閉ざされた門は、内側から開いた。: The closed gate opened from within.
星図の余白に、消えた名前を。: A vanished name in the star chart's margins.
弔鐘の剣姫が、朝への道を塞ぐ。: The sword maiden of the passing bell blocks the way to morning.
リゼットを仲間にし、セリスへつながる最後の記憶を辿る。: Recruit Lisette and follow the final memory leading to Seris.
記憶に囚われた仲間の声を聴き、覚醒への追憶を集める。: Hear companions caught in memory and gather recollections for their awakening.
忘れたはずの夜を、もう一度。: Return once more to the night you thought forgotten.
通常最奥の踏破後に開く追憶。関係者の追憶10個と薄明の剣片6個を確定で仮取得。2: A recollection unlocked after the deepest normal dungeon. Provisionally grants 10 companion memories and 6 Twilight Sword Fragments, with a 20% chance of 12 additional fragments.
追憶・朝を斬った剣: Recollection: The Sword That Cut Morning
あの日の選択を、ひとりに返さない。: Do not leave her alone with the choice of that day.
四人の覚醒後に開く最後の追憶。薄明の剣片12個を確定で仮取得。20%で24個を追: The final recollection, unlocked after four companions awaken. Provisionally grants 12 Twilight Sword Fragments, with a 20% chance of 24 additional fragments.
敵1体の防御を65%無視する攻撃。実際に攻撃を受ける敵が防御低下中なら威力が25: Attacks one enemy, ignoring 65% of Defense. Deals 25% more damage if the enemy actually struck has Defense Down. Prioritized against bosses, weakened enemies, or with Offense strategy.
選択したレアリティの対象がありません。石は消費されません。: No characters are available for the selected rarity. No stones were spent.
出現する女神は選んだシリーズ限定です。重複あり・各レアリティ内は均等抽選です。: Only goddesses from the selected collection can appear. Duplicates are possible; characters of the same rarity have equal odds.
ギリシャ神話の暁の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。朝顔と淡い光を織り込んだ小袖を: A flower-banquet guest inspired by the dawn goddess of Greek mythology. She chose a kosode woven with morning glories and pale light, delighting in the garden's morning dew. Noticing even her companions' smallest steps forward, she gently encourages them. On their journey, she spreads a ward like morning mist and shares the strength to greet a new day.
ギリシャ神話の勝利の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。青緑の羽織に月桂樹と羽根の文: A flower-banquet guest inspired by the victory goddess of Greek mythology. Laurel leaves and feather motifs adorn her teal haori, while festive knotted ribbons play in the breeze. More than grand honors, she delights in seeing a companion achieve what they could not do yesterday. On the road, she breaks obstructing barriers and brings the party a tailwind.
ホームのキャラクターは所持している仲間から選んでください。: Choose a home character from your owned companions.
ホームの表示設定が不正です。: The saved home character setting is invalid.
所持している仲間を選べます。動画のあるキャラはアニメーション、ないキャラは原画を: Choose an owned companion. Characters with animations will move; others display their illustration.
瀬織津姫を着想にした、急流と祓いの女神。氷青の長髪に紙垂を結び、黒と白の礼装で朽: Inspired by Seoritsuhime, goddess of purification and swift rivers. Paper streamers adorn her long ice-blue hair as she stands in black and white robes before a ruined waterfall shrine. The water unwinding from her wand does not erase painful memories. It lets the wounded carry those memories and keep walking.
宇迦之御魂神を女性の姿として描いた、穀物と実りの神。麦金の編み髪と琥珀色の黒レー: An interpretation of the grain deity Ukanomitama as a woman. Wheat-gold braids, amber and black lace, a handful of rice ears, and an old granary key. Long after offerings ceased, she shared the seed rice with a white fox at her feet. Her blessing strengthens her companions and kindles healing to sustain them through a long battle.
弥都波能売神を着想にした、水の女神。紺の短い髪に雨粒の銀飾りを挿し、薄紫と黒の裾: Inspired by Mizuhanome, goddess of water. A silver raindrop pin glints in her short navy hair as her lavender and black skirts brush an ancient bridge. The rain upon her umbrella carries wishes that never reached the river. Her water mirror clouds an enemy's defenses and gently washes away borrowed power.
埴安姫神を着想にした、土と粘土の女神。栗色の横結びと深紅の工房服、金継ぎの走る陶: Inspired by Haniyasuhime, goddess of earth and clay. A chestnut side ponytail, burgundy workwear, and a ceramic shield traced with golden repairs mark her silhouette. Before a ruined kiln, she still fires pots for tiny seedlings. Her shield and protective barriers teach her companions that a crack can be a sign of endurance.
ギリシャ神話の狩猟の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。長い銀の三つ編みに三日月を挿: Inspired by Artemis, Greek goddess of the hunt, and a guest at the Flower Banquet. A crescent adorns her long silver braid, while deer and arrows run in silver thread across her forest-green kimono. The bow she draws in the silent bamboo grove opens a path home. Even an arrow that pierces the strongest armor remembers the lives sleeping in the woods.
ギリシャ神話の春と冥府の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。黒いボブに一筋の紅、葡萄: Inspired by Persephone, Greek goddess of spring and the underworld, and a guest at the Flower Banquet. A crimson streak marks her black bob, and white flowers mingle with roots along her wine-red hem. The pomegranate in her palm is a light to remember the way home. At the border of spring and night, she unravels enemy defenses and borrows a thread of life to stand once more.
帰り灯の小袖: A Lantern to Come Home To
ギリシャ神話の炉の女神を着想にした、花宴への客人。銅赤の髪を低く結び、生成りの小: Inspired by Hestia, Greek goddess of the hearth, and a guest at the Flower Banquet. With copper hair in a low bun, an ivory kimono, and a charcoal haori, she cradles a little lantern. At the edge of the gathering, she is the first to bring warmth to cold hands. Her sheltering back and barriers of lamplight keep a place open for everyone to return.
ギリシャ神話の青春と給仕の女神を着想にした、成人の姿の客人。淡い桃色の髪を高く結: Inspired by Hebe, Greek goddess of youth and cupbearer to the gods, portrayed as an adult guest. Her pale pink hair is tied high above an aqua kimono woven with white cranes as she carries a single cup. She celebrates the courage to take a new step. Her healing cup mends one deep wound, or lets two companions share its comfort for lighter injuries.
月白の衣と銀の飾りを纏い、夜の道を照らす女神。花宴の振袖をしまった日も、仲間を気: Dressed in moon-white cloth and silver ornaments, she lights the roads of night. Even with her banquet furisode put away, her concern for her companions is unchanged. She shares a quiet glow with the wounded and gently guides them somewhere to rest. This is her everyday travelling attire in the world of STILLVEIL.
白い衣に軽い銀の鎧を重ね、梟とともに廃都の地図を読む女神。花宴の華やかな装いとは: Wearing light silver armor over white cloth, she studies the ruined city with an owl at her side. She greets companions in practical travelling clothes rather than her elaborate banquet attire. Reading an enemy's defenses, she chooses a path the party can safely follow. To her, wisdom is a means of protecting someone.
生成りと若草色の素朴なドレスで、朝の庭を手入れする女神。晴れ着を着ない日には、小: In a simple cream and soft green dress, she tends the morning garden. On days without festive clothes, she walks with a little basket of flowers. When she notices someone's wounds or weariness, she chooses a wildflower just for them. Her gentle work continues far beyond the banquet.
白と朱の端正な衣に、小さな日輪の飾りを添えた女神。特別なレースの衣装を離れ、いつ: In an elegant white and vermilion robe with a small sun ornament, she carries the morning light to her companions with her familiar mirror. Away from her special lace costume, she values enough light to see the road ahead over a dazzling display. This is her peaceful travelling form in the world of STILLVEIL.
墨色と生成りの長衣を纏い、静かな水辺に灯をともす女神。特別な黒いレースを脱いでも: In a flowing charcoal and ivory robe, she lights a lantern beside still water. Without her special black lace, her care for travellers remains unchanged. She calms the enemy's momentum and gives her companions a moment to breathe. This peaceful interpretation in the world of STILLVEIL pairs a gentle expression with quiet dignity.
同じ仲間の異なる姿は同時に編成できません。: Different forms of the same companion cannot be in the party together.
通常の姿は全シリーズ共通、衣装版は選んだシリーズ限定です。重複あり・各レアリティ: Base forms appear in every collection; costume forms are exclusive to the selected collection. Duplicates are possible, with equal chances within each rarity.
特別な装いを離れた、女神たちのいつもの姿。どのシリーズからも迎えられます。: The goddesses in their everyday attire, away from special costumes. Available in every collection.
表示は通常時の基準値です。SSR確率上昇中はR・SRの確率も変動し、SSR保証時: These are the normal base chances. R and SR chances change during increased SSR odds; guaranteed SSR wishes do not draw from the shared pool.
通常の姿と特別な装いは別々に迎えられます。同じ女神の異なる姿は同時に編成できませ: Base and costume forms are acquired separately. Different forms of the same goddess cannot be in the party together.
銀の三つ編みを揺らし、森の小径を歩く女神。いつもの緑の旅装に弓を携え、獣の足跡か: With her silver braid and familiar green travel clothes, she follows forest paths with a bow at her side. Animal tracks show her the safest way through the ruins. When her companions lose their way at night, she leaves a little light before offering a word.
黒い短髪に小さな柘榴の飾りを添えた女神。深紅の旅衣で枯れた庭を巡り、まだ眠ってい: A small pomegranate ornament rests in her short black hair. In a burgundy travelling dress, she gathers sleeping seeds from abandoned gardens. She slows her foes and gives her companions time to recover, teaching them the strength of waiting for a new season.
帰り道の灯火: A Light for the Way Home
栗色の髪と素朴な前掛けが似合う女神。旅先で見つけた古い宿に火を入れ、誰でも休める: With chestnut hair and a simple apron, she rekindles the hearths of abandoned inns so anyone can rest. In battle, she raises warm barriers like lantern light, protecting her companions with a small shield and a generous sense of safety.
桃色の髪を高く結び、青い旅衣で水辺を歩く女神。休憩のたびに小さな茶器を取り出し、: Her pink ponytail bobs above a blue travelling dress as she walks beside the water. At every rest stop, she unpacks a little tea set and offers a warm cup. This dependable travelling companion reaches out to two wounded friends at once.
淡い桃色の髪に朝の光を映す女神。軽い外套と灯りを携え、まだ暗い丘を仲間と越えてい: Morning light catches in her pale peach hair. With a light cape and lantern, she crosses dark hills alongside her companions. A following breeze lifts their spirits and clears their weariness as they search for daybreak together.
青緑の三つ編みに月桂の葉を留めた女神。白い旅衣に軽い鎧を重ね、剣の手入れを欠かさ: Laurel leaves adorn her dark teal braid. She wears light armour over a white travelling tunic and carefully tends her sword. Bringing everyone home matters more to her than a hurried victory, so she breaks barriers to open a path for her friends.
紫の髪と小さな郵便鞄が目印の女神。薄紫の旅衣で廃都を渡り、途絶えた手紙を届けてい: Her purple hair and little mail satchel are familiar sights among the ruins. In lavender travel clothes, she carries letters that never reached their destinations. A rainbow puts a spring in her step. She unravels enemy enhancements and brings hopeful news to her friends.
藍色の長い髪に真珠を一粒飾った女神。穏やかな海色の衣で浜辺を歩き、貝の器に澄んだ: A single pearl rests in her long indigo hair. In robes the colour of a calm sea, she walks the shore and gathers clear water in a shell bowl. Gentle healing waves and a thin barrier of water help travellers reach the next shore.
ぜんまいを巻いたら、あたしの時間！: Wind the key, and it's my turn!
ボスは3ターンごとにうさぎビットを展開。翌ターンから2ターン、各ビットが味方1人: The boss deploys Rabbit Bits every 3 turns. Starting on the following turn, each bit automatically shoots one companion for 2 turns. Barriers, guarding, and damage reduction help; defeating the boss stops the bits. As a companion, Lunette uses area attacks and barriers. The bits are a boss-only ability.
大時計が目覚める夜、もう一度遊ぼう。: When the great clock awakens, let us play once more.
うさぎたちの行進が、静かな庭を起こす。: A parade of rabbits wakes the silent garden.
3ターンごとにビット展開、翌ターンから2ターン射撃。展開中に障壁やかばうを用意し: Bits deploy every 3 turns and fire for 2 turns starting on the next turn. Prepare barriers and guards while they deploy. Confirm the materials you earn to welcome Lunette as a companion.
ふふふっ、おねえさんよっわー: Hee-hee! You're sooo weak, big sis!
むぅ……うさぎ隊、もっと本気でいくよ！: Hmph... Rabbit squad, let's get serious!
ま、負けてないし……もう一回、遊んでくれる？: I-I didn't lose... Will you play with me again?
星時計、ぜんまい全開！ あたしのうさぎ隊についてこれる？: Star-clock, fully wound! Can you keep up with my rabbit squad?
ふふっ、やるじゃん！ ここからが本番だよ！: Hee-hee, you're pretty good! Now the real game begins!
……強いね、おねえさん。次は、あたしも連れてって。: ...You're strong, big sis. Next time, take me with you.
忘れられた時計庭に住む、小柄な発明家の少女。得意げな言葉とは裏腹に、壊れたうさぎ: A petite young inventor lives in a forgotten clockwork garden. Despite her boastful words, she cannot leave a broken rabbit behind. Surrounded by her handmade mechanical rabbits, she invites passing travellers to play. She has long been waiting for a promise to go home together.
大時計の奥で眠っていた星のぜんまいが、少女とうさぎたちの願いに応える。紺と白の旅: A star-wound spring sleeping within the great clock answers the wishes of a girl and her rabbits. Star gears adorn her navy and ivory travelling clothes as she promises never to leave anyone behind. Even her cheeky laughter becomes a way to make sure her companions are still close.
